classification.difficultyReason: Interpret intercepts, tangencies and centre guides to identify each circle, then construct its equation; part (d) requires using the distance from (1,1) to the origin to obtain the radius.

content.prompt: Find the centre, radius and equation of the following circles.

spec.description: Circle with horizontal intercepts −4 and 2, midpoint tick −1, and positive axis arrows. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the supplied circle are visible.

answer.worked:
The centre is midway between the horizontal intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{-4+2}{2}=-1\\r&=2-(-1)=3\end{align*}$$
The centre is $(-1,0)$, so the equation is
$$(x+1)^2+y^2=9.$$

spec.description: Circle tangent to the y-axis; dashed guides show x=2, y=−1 and y=−3. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Centre guides and source labels are supplied; no equation is shown.

answer.worked:
The dashed guides give the centre $(2,-3)$. The top of the circle has $y=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}r&=-1-(-3)\\r&=2\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$(x-2)^2+(y+3)^2=4.$$

spec.description: Circle touches the x-axis at −1 and y-axis at 1. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source tangencies and tick labels are supplied.

answer.worked:
The circle touches the axes at $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, so its centre is $(-1,1)$ and its radius is $1$.
$$(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2=1.$$

spec.description: Circle through the origin and the axis intercepts 2; dashed centre guides at x=1 and y=1. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied guides and intercepts remain visible; radius and equation are responses.

answer.worked:
The guides give the centre $(1,1)$. Using the origin on the circle,
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=(1-0)^2+(1-0)^2\\r^2&=2\\r&=\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=2.$$
